## Project Overview
This repository is an ESP-IDF firmware project targeting the ESP32-C3 (RISC-V) with the following conventions:
- Source code lives in `main/`; entry point is `app_main()` in [main/hello_world_main.c](../main/hello_world_main.c)
- Build config lives in the root [CMakeLists.txt](../CMakeLists.txt) and [main/CMakeLists.txt](../main/CMakeLists.txt) via `idf_component_register`
- Python integration tests live in the repo root (e.g. [pytest_hello_world.py](../pytest_hello_world.py)), using `pytest-embedded`
- Generated build artifacts live in `build/` and are never hand-edited

## Commands
- Build: using cmake. The root CMakeLists.txt file is located in the project root directory.
- Flash + monitor: using `idf.py -p PORT flash monitor`
- Size report: using `idf.py size`
- Set target: using `idf.py set-target esp32c3`
- Run tests: using `pytest pytest_hello_world.py` (requires `pytest-embedded` and IDF env)

## Coding Conventions
- Use C with ESP-IDF APIs; follow the style already present in [main/hello_world_main.c](../main/hello_world_main.c).
- Source files use the SPDX license header (`CC0-1.0`) as seen in [main/hello_world_main.c](../main/hello_world_main.c).
- New source files go under `main/`
- Every new code component should be placed in a dedicated directory under `main/` to maintain modularity and organization. The component must be associated with its own CMakeLists.txt for proper integration.
- Component dependencies are declared via `PRIV_REQUIRES`/`REQUIRES` in `main/CMakeLists.txt`, not via manual include paths.
- Keep functions focused on a single responsibility and use meaningful names for functions, variables, and files.

## Agent Expectations
- Do not edit generated files under `build/` — they are regenerated by `idf.py build`.
- Verify changes by using `cmake` before considering a task complete.
- Keep changes minimal, safe, and aligned with the commands and conventions above.
